solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Where farmer might be without men skilled and obstinate

indicators.note: without says the letters for men are dropped from the phrase

parts.note: a farmer might be sitting in a tractor, written as a phrase
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for ordinary soldiers or men
skilled means able

explanation.surface: A stubborn, capable farmer who somehow manages without any farmhands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops OR (other ranks, i.e. men) from IN TRACTOR, leaving INTRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an obstinate person or problem is stubborn and hard to manage or control.

clue.text: Eureka! The setter's got sex appeal!

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, and 'has got' becomes have
IT is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A boastful setter crowing that he is irresistible.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclamation equivalence: Archimedes' cry 'Eureka!' means 'I have found it', a shout of discovery.

clue.text: Teacher's badly out, entering first two consonants in turn

indicators.note: entering puts the jumbled letters between the two consonants

parts.note: the opening two consonants of the word turn are T and R

indicators.note: badly says the letters of out are jumbled

explanation.surface: A teacher has been poorly treated and must leave, taking turns with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in turn' looks like 'one after another'; here it says which word supplies the two consonants.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a private teacher, or a university supervisor, is a tutor.

clue.text: Deal with spy protecting mere criminal

indicators.note: protecting means the spy wraps around the jumbled letters

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: criminal says the letters of mere are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deal is struck with a secret agent to shield a petty criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a deal between parties is an agreement or arrangement.

clue.text: Change of heart for Boris, say, in ancient city

indicators.note: the heart of the word is altered: its two middle letters swap places

parts.note: Boris Johnson, the former UK prime minister, is an example of a Tory (Conservative)

explanation.surface: A politician has a change of mind while visiting an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters OR of TORY swap to RO. Boris Johnson was a Conservative prime minister of the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the city besieged by the Greeks in Homer's Iliad is the classic ancient city.

clue.text: This source of funds he arranged could give back-hander

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the answer and of he are mixed together to give back-hander

explanation.surface: A man could fiddle a source of funds to produce a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the answer plus HE, 'arranged', gives the letters of BACKHANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a bank card lets its holder draw money, so it is a source of funds.

clue.text: Leave banker by accident on vacation

parts.note: a banker in crosswords is a river, something with banks; the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: on vacation means the word is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A banker takes leave after an accident while away on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties ACCIDENT to AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-friendly sense: an exeat is permission for leave of absence, as from a school or college.

clue.text: Keep an eye on old vicar promoted by diocese

indicators.note: promoted means raised up, read upward in this down clue

parts.note: a vicar is addressed as Rev, short for Reverend
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: An elderly vicar is promoted within his diocese to supervise others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns REV upward in the down light to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to oversee work is to supervise or watch over it.

clue.text: Slowcoach trained me and you, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the phrase is heard, giving a word of similar sound

parts.note: trained means taught; me and you means us

explanation.surface: Someone who taught two people is said to have been a slow learner.
explanation.walkthrough: A nod to Lewis Carroll's Mock Turtle: 'We called him Tortoise because he taught us.'
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tortoise is proverbially slow, as in the fable of the race with the hare.

clue.text: PM following nobody when European quits

parts.note: following means after

indicators.note: quits means a letter walks out of the phrase

parts.note: nobody means no one

explanation.surface: A prime minister follows no one once a European leaves the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' looks like prime minister; it is post meridiem.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: p.m. (post meridiem) marks the hours after midday.

clue.text: As lovers, take flight, actor Keith avoiding writer

indicators.note: avoiding means the writer is left out

parts.note: Penelope Keith is a British actress, star of the TV sitcom The Good Life
a pen is a writer, the instrument one writes with

explanation.surface: Penelope Keith runs off with a lover, dodging a pursuing author.
explanation.walkthrough: Penelope Keith is a British actress known for the 1970s sitcom The Good Life.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic use: lovers who elope run away secretly together, usually to marry.

clue.text: Student mislaying letter of representation, something fairly lucrative

indicators.note: mislaying says one letter is lost

parts.note: a learner is a student
L is the letter that represents a learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A student loses a letter of reference, yet still has a nice little earner.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the British symbol for a learner driver, shown on L-plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British usage: a nice little earner is a moneymaker, something profitable.

clue.text: More than one film star's touring gallery

indicators.note: touring means going around the gallery, enclosing it

parts.note: a star is an ace; the 's adds an S
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A film star is touring an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: Acetate is a type of plastic sheet used for photographic film.
explanation.definitionFit: Material sense: acetate is a cellulose sheet used as photographic film, so acetates are films.

clue.text: Something with three legs? Time against Bolt!

parts.note: a rivet is a metal bolt

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt racing the clock, and something with three legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' suggests the sprinter Usain Bolt; it is a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a trivet is a stand, typically with three feet, for a hot pot.

clue.text: Our silly novel is unreal

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A silly novel of ours is unrealistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something illusory is deceptive or imaginary, not real.

clue.text: Lead Greek character drawn in by bars

indicators.note: drawn in by means the Greek letter is held within the bars

parts.note: a grate is a set of bars
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A lead Greek character is sketched in a bar scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like leading; it is the metal sense, pencil lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Material sense: pencil lead is made of graphite, a form of carbon.

clue.text: Stopped playing around on … on ice?

indicators.note: playing around says the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Someone stopped fooling around on an ice rink.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: plans put on ice are deferred or shelved for later.

clue.text: Free emperor kidnapped by group, both using the same name

indicators.note: kidnapped by means the emperor is held inside the group

parts.note: a genus is a group in biological classification

indicators.note: the group and the emperor share one N, the abbreviation for name, so the emperor's N is not written twice

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An emperor seized by a gang with the same name is set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both using the same name' means GENUS and NERO share a single N (name): GEN + ERO + US, so NERO loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: free with money or time means generous, liberal.

clue.text: With copper standing by, a large number delivered clothes

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: delivered means spoken, so the words are heard

parts.note: a large number is lots

explanation.surface: A policeman stands by as a delivery of clothes arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman; it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: culottes are women's knee-length trousers cut like a skirt, a type of clothing.

clue.text: Advise no clue's to be tweaked

indicators.note: tweaked means adjusted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is told to fix a clue that isn't working.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to counsel someone is to give them guidance.

clue.text: View a ghost about to vanish

indicators.note: to vanish says these letters disappear

parts.note: a spectre is a ghost
re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A view of a ghost about to vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an aspect is a view, as of a house facing a direction.

clue.text: Annoy Republican exiting during explosive function

indicators.note: during means inside the explosive

parts.note: TNT is an explosive

indicators.note: exiting means leaving the word

parts.note: anger means annoy

explanation.surface: A Republican leaves in annoyance at an explosive event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' here is the trigonometric kind, not an event or party.
explanation.definitionFit: Maths sense: tangent is a trigonometric function, alongside sine and cosine.

clue.text: Aboard submarine maybe, with the German leaving light cap off?

indicators.note: leaving says those letters go

parts.note: aboard a submarine, one would be under the sea
der is a German word for the
an LED is a light

explanation.surface: On a submarine, a German leaves after a light lid comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes DER from UNDERSEA, giving UNSEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a bottle with its cap off is open, no longer sealed.

clue.text: Answer boss, being forward

parts.note: a head is a boss

explanation.surface: Answering the boss with forward manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: forward, in front, means in advance.

clue.text: Alternative medicine sending oxygen to the head?

indicators.note: sending says a letter is moved
to the head means to the front of the word

parts.note: a potion is a medicinal drink
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Alternative medicine that sends oxygen to the brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative medicine' reads as one phrase; split it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an alternative is a choice, one of the options available.

clue.text: Furious Spock's second to abandon Bones, perhaps

indicators.note: to abandon says that letter leaves

parts.note: Billy Bones is a pirate in Treasure Island

indicators.note: second means the second letter of Spock's

explanation.surface: Spock's deputy walks out on Bones, the Star Trek doctor, angrily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' suggests Dr McCoy in Star Trek, beside Spock; it is Billy Bones from Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: furious means very angry.

clue.text: Branch makes withdrawal from capital I'm banking

indicators.note: a withdrawal takes some letters from the phrase, inside it

explanation.surface: A bank branch makes a withdrawal from its capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a branch of a tree is a limb.

clue.text: Peers involved in bout of self-indulgence

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peers caught up in an indulgent spending bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a spree is a bout of indulgence, like a shopping binge.

clue.text: Establish position unsettling to trainee

indicators.note: unsettling means disturbing, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Establishing a new job position unsettles the trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to orientate is to find one's bearings, locating oneself.

clue.text: Naughty daughter isn't accepting order to stop working

indicators.note: accepting means taking in the other pieces

parts.note: isn't is written ISNT, dropping the apostrophe
the OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire
to die is to stop working, as a battery

explanation.surface: A naughty daughter isn't taking an order to stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: naughty children are badly behaved, refusing to obey.
